note: Every public source found for org.telegram.messenger, org.telegram.messenger.web and org.telegram.messenger.beta, with the branches and commits it was last read at, its licence and what HushTelegram may take from it. scripts/telegram-sources.ps1 holds it to its rules, scripts/audit-telegram-sources.ps1 refreshes it, and a local release needs a census from the last 14 days. docs/sources.md is the readable version. Since 2026-10-17, Premium unlocks, ways past content protection, content Telegram hides as sensitive and a higher account limit count as open ideas, and one that goes past another person's setting can only ship as a default-off switch. Naming an idea in a reason never means its code is adopted.

entries.reason: The oldest Telegram patch set found: its history starts 2026-04-17, four months before anyone else's, and the ads, content and premium layout and the patch names reappear in rushiranpise's bundle. Pinned to telegram.org's 12.8.3. Half its list unlocks Premium or gets past a channel's restrictions, open ideas, not adopted code. Disable auto update and Download speed boost are the ideas worth checking against 12.10.6. The indexes also list it for org.telegram.messenger, but its own patch list declares only the web build at 12.8.3, so no version is recorded for the store package.

The pinned set has 14 patches for standard and web Telegram 12.10.1, and 15 for Plus Messenger. The features list is their union, not a count for each package. Its signature chain seeds Telegram's DER certificate and answers Telegram's fingerprint check and Firebase's certificate hash. HushTelegram's current source instead uses a fresh implementation scoped to the Firebase Installations X-Android-Cert header, with the certificate digest verified from the official fixture and with existing callback and header bindings checked before insertion. Fixture and runtime tests verify that scope. Genuine push registration still needs a device comparison. No signature-chain code was adopted. Listing a feature does not approve it for HushTelegram. Its Premium, restriction bypass and anti-screenshot-notification patches are open ideas, not adopted code.

rushiranpise's Telegram set carried on under a third name and retargeted to 12.10.4. Its Remove ads adds fingerprints for the messages controller's sponsored request and response and for the video ads loader, the same two places HushTelegram's Hide ads found on its own in 12.10.6. Its README and target notes still say 12.10.3; patches-list.json is the one to believe. A side branch, fix/telegram-12.10.3-70892, retargets the same patches to Telegram 12.10.3 build 70892 (new ActionBar and typing-dispatcher fingerprints, a different checkCanOpenChat overload and rich-paste handlers). It adds no new feature.

mirrors.reason: The same bundle's earlier name; its commits still link there. Gone (404) by 2026-09-30, a snapshot is in the Morphe Archive.
The same bundle under another name, gone (404) by 2026-09-30. Known only from the Morphe Archive's snapshot.

entries.reason: A one-time copy of rushiranpise's set from 2026-08-19, before the certificate fix: its cert seed patch is commented out and it embeds the whole PKCS7 block. Nothing in it the live bundle doesn't do better. Its dev branch is a later reshuffle of the same copy. It brings back Disable analytics and drops the Premium UI and Plus patches. It adds no new idea.

Written separately from the Paresh lineage, in the older ReVanced fingerprint style, and quiet since 2026-03-23. It declares no Telegram build, so nothing says which version it last worked on. It reached the same signature and integrity anchors on its own, which is good evidence they're the right ones. Its dev and patcher-v22 branches port the same Telegram patches to patcher v22 with updated fingerprints. They add no feature.

An independent set verified against 12.10.1, built on patcher 1.8.0, with fingerprints that fail loudly rather than patch the wrong method. Disable story read marking and Remove promo channels are worth checking. Most of the rest unlocks Premium or gets past content protection, open ideas, not adopted code. Its README says it leaves out anti-delete and ghost mode on purpose. Its latest change declares Telegram 12.10.1 as a concrete target for the store, web and beta builds alike.

An Xposed module that hooks Telegram at run time, quiet since 2025-04-21. Hide Stories and Prohibit channel switching are the ideas worth rewriting as patches. Anti anti-forward gets past a channel's forward protection, so it could only come back as a default-off switch. A port means reimplementing the idea, not copying hooks.

The best-known single-purpose module for Telegram's sponsored messages, which shows how much people want them gone. Its second feature gets past a channel's save restriction. HushTelegram's default-off switch for files and songs from those chats is its own code.

mirrors.reason: A copy of Killergram that is not a GitHub fork. Its hook class moved to its own package name and the rest follows the original.

entries.reason: A Killergram rewrite with additional camera and UI hooks. Lazy attachment-camera preview construction is a candidate for keeping gallery selection separate from camera initialization. The pinned Xposed hooks are research references, not maintained dependencies or accepted HushTelegram features. Its restricted-content saving is an idea only, and HushTelegram's default-off switch for files and songs is its own code.

The GitLab home of the Paresh lineage that MoonShadowKeeper, rushiranpise and their copies carry on, with 31 forks. It patches the web build at 12.9.2 and 12.8.3 and Plus Messenger at 12.9.2. The GitLab commit listing needs a token, so no watch path is set and any new commit on a branch counts as a change. Its list shares the lineage's Premium and restriction bypass patches, open ideas, not adopted code. The ads, auto update, typing indicator and speed ideas are already covered by the other copies.

mirrors.reason: The GitHub address Awesome Morphe lists for this project. It answers 404 today, and the code lives on GitLab.

entries.reason: A GitHub copy of the Paresh set from May, pinned to telegram.org's web build 12.6.4. Every patch in it also exists, newer, in the other copies of the lineage, so there is nothing here to take. Its dev branch is the lineage's test line and holds the same Telegram patches, mixed with work on unrelated apps.

rushiranpise's set retargeted to Telegram 13.0.1 for the store and web builds (Plus Messenger stays on 12.10.6.0). That makes it the first copy of the lineage on 13.x, so its fingerprints are worth comparing with the ones HushTelegram needs for 13.0.1. The features list is the union across packages. Its Premium, restriction bypass and anti-screenshot-notification patches are open ideas, not adopted code.

A general bundle with one Telegram patch, Anti-disappearing media, built on the Paresh lineage's fingerprints. Its patch list declares only the web build, at 12.8.3 and 12.10.1. The indexes list the store package too. The patch exists in every other copy of the lineage, so there is nothing new here.

A general bundle that carries the Paresh Telegram set for the web build at 12.8.3 and Plus Messenger at 12.7.3.0. It also commits its compiled build output. Everything in it exists, newer, in the other copies of the lineage.
A general bundle whose only Telegram patch unlocks Premium on 12.10.1, one of the open ideas, not adopted code.

An independent bundle of 457 patches, marked experimental and described by its author as written by AI, with five Telegram patches and no declared Telegram version. Block ads and hide stories, Disable proximity sensor and the pinned chats limit are the ideas to look at. Saving restricted media and Premium are open ideas, not adopted code.

A font bundle for readability and accessibility, with one Telegram patch that forces the system font. It declares 12.10.6 for the store build and 12.10.5 for the web build. The idea is worth weighing as an accessibility option.

An earlier copy of Aunali321's ReVanced Telegram patches, last pushed in February 2025, with some files that differ from the live ones. It declares no Telegram build. Nothing in it that the original doesn't do better. Its dev branch, and two Dependabot branches cut from it, share no history with main. They hold the same Telegram patches.

An Xposed module for third-party Telegram clients. Its hook entry lists the official store, web and beta packages beside Plus Messenger and a long list of forks, which settles the earlier doubt about official Telegram. Show message ID, Prohibit channel switching and Hide sponsored messages are the ideas worth rewriting as patches. Anti anti-forward and Anti anti-copy get past a channel's protection, so they could only come back as default-off switches. A port means reimplementing an idea, not copying hooks.

mirrors.reason: A detached copy of cinit/TMoe whose hook entry and startup hook match it file for file.
A release-build copy of TMoe whose hook entry and startup hook match it file for file.

entries.reason: An April 2024 copy of TMoe on a dev branch, with an Anti-delete messages hook added to the original. It has not moved since. Nothing else is new, so the original is the one to read. Its main branch carries the 2023 TMoe history with newer hooks than the dev branch.

features: Remove the Archived Chats button and pull-down gesture
entries.reason: A small Xposed module from 2022 that removes the Archived Chats button and its pull-down gesture from the chat list. A quiet-mode idea. Untouched since 2022.

An Xposed module for official Telegram with no licence, so none of its code can be read for porting. Its ad blocking and pinned-message hiding show what people ask for. Its forwarding and saving switches get past protection, and with no licence they stay ideas only.
A 2022 hook project against Telegram 8.7.4 with no licence. It adds a repeat plus-one button, anti-recall and a screenshot unlock. Too old to say anything about current builds.

An Xposed module that hides your own phone number on screen. It is AGPL-3.0, which can't be combined with HushTelegram's GPL-3.0, so only what it does is usable. The idea is simple to rediscover from Telegram's own code.
A one-hook module with no licence that tunes FileLoadOperation to speed up downloads. The same idea is in several bundles already.

The Xposed Modules Repo copy of TeleSpeed, which hooks download parameters. Download speed boost is already covered by better documented patches, so it adds nothing. A libxposed branch rewrites the same hook for the newer Xposed API.
A 2021 module that blocks sponsored messages and nothing else. Killergram does the same job and is better documented.
A simple module that turns the Stories feature off in official Telegram. Tested on 10.10.0 and quiet since 2024. The idea of hiding stories is worth checking against current builds.

features: Anti-delete messages with a deleted flag
entries.reason: An Xposed module with an anti-delete hook that marks the message with its own deleted flag, a repeat plus-one menu item, and a copy and save unlock. The README warns that updating may lose all chat history. The flag approach is worth studying. The copy and save unlock gets past protection, so it could only come back as a default-off switch.
A 2022 module with no licence that blocks sponsored messages and clears the secure window flag so screenshots work. Nothing here that other sources don't show.

A personal-preference module with no licence. It hides the bottom tabs, changes swipe and double-tap behavior and adjusts Stories. It targets the current Telegram layout (MainTabsActivity), so it shows what a patch for the new tab bar would hit.

features: Replace emoji with Noto, EmojiOne or Twemoji
entries.reason: A 2017 module with no licence that swaps Telegram's emoji set. Far too old to be a reference for current builds.
An MIT-licensed LSPosed module from 2025 aimed at official Telegram. Hiding online, seen and typing status is the ghost mode idea. Its Premium unlock is one of the open ideas, not adopted code.

An Apache-2.0 LSPosed module from September 2026 that restyles the Google Play build's bottom bar and chat chrome at run time. It is a visual theme, but it shows which current classes a UI patch would reach.

features: Set the secure flag on every window
entries.reason: A tiny module that forces the secure window flag on every Telegram window, which blocks screenshots and hides the app in the recents list. A privacy option, and the opposite of a bypass. Last changed in 2023.

A 2022 MIT-licensed module that removes forwarding restrictions, fakes Premium and clears the secure window flag. All three are open ideas, not adopted code, and the two that go past another person's setting could only come back as default-off switches.

features: Hide blacklisted messages in the chat adapter
entries.reason: A 2019 module with no licence that hooks the chat adapter's row builder to filter messages from a blacklist. Too old to say anything about current builds.

features: Disable animated emoji and image animations
entries.reason: A 2022 module that turns off animations by hooking ImageReceiver and AnimatedEmojiDrawable. It is AGPL-3.0, which can't be combined with HushTelegram's GPL-3.0, so only what it does is usable. It has no package check of its own, so it works on whatever Telegram client the user scopes it to.

The Paresh lineage ported to Telegram 12.10.5 on its dev and port branches, while main is still the stock Morphe template, which is why the indexes list it with an empty patch list. The port rebuilds the fingerprints for 12.10.5 (the ChatActivity sponsored-slot methods moved into an obfuscated class) and ships a bytecode audit and a fingerprint matrix. It adds Disable rich HTML paste, Enable translations, High quality stories and Stories features to the lineage's set, and targets Plus Messenger 12.10.1.1 and the web build 12.10.1. The audit documents are the useful part. Its Premium, restriction bypass and anti-screenshot-notification patches are open ideas, not adopted code.

outOfScope.reason: ReVanced has never had a Telegram patch: no telegram path exists in its history on dev or main.

Telegram's own source (GPL-2.0-or-later), pinned at f2908b1 for 12.10.6. It's a behavior reference, not a patch source or adopted code. BuildVars, phone and passkey authentication, ConnectionsManager and the binary manifest establish the bindings used by HushTelegram's fresh optional API and Maps credential patches. Configured fixture tests and a signed CLI proof on web 12.10.6 change only the APP_ID and APP_HASH initialization literals and the Maps SDK key metadata. All 118,949 method declarations, native libraries and resource-table values remain intact. Both patches leave the original credentials untouched when options are unset. Telegram issues registered API credentials through my.telegram.org/apps, and Google requires the Maps Android SDK key to authorize the installed package and signer. No real credentials or live service authorization were tested.

Google's official Android SDK is a maintained implementation reference, not a Telegram patch source or adopted code. The pinned FirebaseInstallationServiceClient computes the installed package's SHA-1 certificate fingerprint and sends it in X-Android-Cert alongside X-Android-Package. This establishes the narrow header binding checked by HushTelegram's fresh Firebase repair. The inspected root license is Apache-2.0 at https://github.com/firebase/firebase-android-sdk/blob/53c7411df8fb5c577b8d898ead74d087c1cc8f2b/LICENSE, with SHA-256 cfc7749b96f63bd31c3c42b5c471bf756814053e847c10f3eb003417bc523d30. No SDK source was copied or adopted. Genuine push registration still needs a device comparison.
ReVanced patches run through Xposed. No Telegram path in its tree.
Telegram X, a separate open source client on TDLib. No patch bundle exists for it and HushTelegram doesn't target it.

A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source or a HushTelegram dependency. Hide Stories (NekoConfig.hideStories in StoriesController) and its download speed boost are research candidates. A listed feature still needs its own behavior and privacy review.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. Combine messages and forced plain-text copy are its distinct ideas.

A Telegram fork with its own package. Its repository was verified archived on 2026-10-01, but the archive date is unknown. The pinned dev branch and paste/transfer reports are historical research references, not evidence of current maintenance or a HushTelegram dependency.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. The most active of the Nagram line.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. Hide Stories and ads. Its tracker has several ghost mode requests closed without being built.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. showOnlineStatus and hideStories switches, the closest thing to a ghost mode in a live fork.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. Tracks upstream closely (12.10.6). A build base for other forks, few features.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. Quiet since 2025-01-03, on 9.6.6. Known for its plugin system.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. The Android port of AyuGram, quiet since 2023-09-11. The ghost mode and saved-deletions ideas live on in desktop AyuGram.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. Quiet since 2023-03-18.
A Telegram fork, a whole client with its own package, so not a patch source. An active Nagram-line fork.

elsewhere.reason: A bundle for the ReSeam patch engine (.reseam files, not Morphe) on the project's own Forgejo server, AGPL-3.0-or-later with section 7 terms since 2026-10-06. Its Telegram part targets 12.10.6: hide sponsored ads, a download boost, push notifications after re-signing by spoofing the signature, an integrity bypass, screenshots, a deleted-message archive, restriction and forward-from-restricted bypasses, hiding the typing indicator, removing Play Store restrictions, Unlock Pro and turning off auto-update (read through the Forgejo API at e629ca4, 2026-10-10). Recorded for reference only. The bypasses, the deleted-message archive and Unlock Pro stay out under HushTelegram's rules, and a different engine's code isn't ported.
